 / Cybersecurity World Liberty Financial Freezes $27 Million in USD1 After Binance Transfers
 World Liberty Financial froze $27 million in USD1 linked to the Binance hot wallet transfers. Zach Witkoff confirmed the proactive freeze.
 Andrew Samu Published 30 Oct 2026 • 1 min read 
 World Liberty Financial has frozen $27 million in its USD1 stablecoin linked to the transfers out of Binance hot wallets. Chief executive Zach Witkoff said the company took the step proactively.
 Witkoff wrote: “USD1 has taken proactive steps to freeze the $27 million in USD1 associated with the @binance hack. We stand by our industry partners. Protecting users and preventing bad actors from moving stolen funds is a shared responsibility.” 
 Binance co-CEO Yi He thanked the World Liberty Financial team for the freeze and also noted roughly $2 million in the related WLFI token had been frozen. The action sits alongside larger freezes by Tether and Circle. Binance has confirmed a verified total of $2.54 billion frozen so far and has said user funds remain safe while it continues its review.
 USD1 is a smaller issuer than USDT or USDC, so the absolute amount is modest relative to the overall outflows. The freeze still shows the same pattern: stablecoin issuers can block balances once addresses are identified, while non-freezable assets such as ether cannot.
 Author: Andy Samu
